title: envelope backpressure and deterministic tool_choice error schema
author: Anika Bose
release_notes: Introduces a deterministic tool_choice error schema and streaming envelope backpressure indicator; clients should tolerate new optional fields. Non-breaking for existing OpenAI-compat consumers.
description:
Context and motivation: We observed nondeterministic tool selection and silent failures when downstream tool processes returned transient backpressure (rate-limit / overload) during streaming tool/function invocations. This manifested as partial tool messages, missing tool_choice resolutions, and inconsistent retry behaviors across SDKs. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: 1) a deterministic error schema for tool_choice resolution so callers can programmatically react to selection failures, and 2) an explicit envelope-level backpressure indicator that can be emitted during streaming to signal temporary unavailability of a tool and a suggested retry window.

What this changes (high level):
- Add `tool_choice_error` object to OpenAI-compat invoke responses and stream fragments. The object is deterministic (fields: code, reason, suggested_retry_ms) and is emitted when the platform cannot finalize a tool assignment due to capacity or schema mismatch.
- Add envelope-level field `backpressure_hint_ms` to streaming fragments (optional integer). When present clients should postpone immediate retries of the same tool for the specified window.
- Make streaming fragments emit explicit boundary frames around tool messages to avoid partial payload confusion in the client. Boundary frames are idempotent markers and do not change payload semantics.
- Update compatibility adapter to map internal executor backpressure/error states into the new OpenAI-compatible fields.
- SDK and docs updates: python and typescript SDKs updated to surface the new fields with improved parsing helpers and examples.

Review conversation (high level):
- Liam: requested a deterministic error code set and suggested using single byte markers for boundaries to keep bandwidth low. Also asked for metrics (counter for backpressure events).
- Anika: added error codes (TOOL_UNAVAILABLE, TOOL_SCHEMA_MISMATCH, TOOL_TIMEOUT) and added a low-entropy one-byte boundary marker; pushed an extra commit adding metrics.backpressure_events counter.
- Jin: flagged potential client breakage if SDKs assume no extra fields. Requested SDK tests and migration notes. Anika added SDK parsing helpers, unit tests, and the docs migration note.
- Marta: ran perf canary and requested microbenchmark numbers. Anika added a microbenchmark and updated the PR with results (median overhead < 1.2% on steady-state streaming workloads).
- Final: reviewers approved after fixes; CI green.
